solves.reasoning: Voice resonates (공감) with readers makes sense; clashes would mean conflict. Brand should be memorable, not forgettable. Distinct from competitors, not similar. All three original words fit.
Pinpointing (precisely locating) target audience is the entrepreneurial strategy. Alien = the concepts feel foreign to scholars. Innovative ideas, not common — Labaree emphasizes novelty.
Literature review aims to highlight (not obscure) research gaps. These are overlooked (not celebrated) areas. The voice should be distinctive (not ordinary). All original.
Conceal contradicts the scholarly purpose — you highlight gaps to justify your research, not conceal them. The other three words fit their contexts perfectly.
Identical from competitors is semantically wrong — you want to be distinct, not identical. Alien, gaps, distinctive all fit their contexts.
Abandoning the expression of ideas contradicts the passage's message about balancing expression with voice development. The other three are contextually correct.
Building a brand — the passage discusses branding strategy. Audience is mentioned separately, budget and schedule are irrelevant.
Highlight gaps in research — this is the core of literature review. Strengths/achievements would negate the need for new research.
Cultivating a distinctive voice — developing/nurturing a voice. Suppressing, imitating, abandoning all contradict the goal.
Resonates with = connects with. The voice connects/relates to readers. Fades/conflicts/disappears are opposite or unrelated.
Pinpointing = identifying precisely. Overlooking means missing, dismissing means rejecting, broadening means expanding — none mean precise identification.
Alien in this context = unfamiliar/foreign. Not familiar (that's opposite), not essential, not appealing.
Distinct = distinguishable, so opposite = indistinguishable. Unique/prominent/remarkable are synonyms, not antonyms.
Overlooked = ignored/unnoticed. Opposite = scrutinized (carefully examined). Neglected/abandoned/forgotten are synonyms of overlooked.
(A) Drawing customers to products = attracting/끌어들이다. (B) Drawing the sunset with pencils = sketching/그리다. Clear polysemy.
The definition describes proposition — a statement proposing value/benefit. Competition = rivalry, impression = mark left, expression = conveying thoughts.
Article 'a' + blank + noun 'identity' = adjective needed. Recognize → recognizable (able to be recognized).
'the' + blank + 'of' = noun needed. Express (verb) → expression (noun). The expression of your ideas.
Scholars set themselves apart in their academic writing — the passage explicitly connects scholarly and entrepreneurial practices in writing contexts.
Crafting a unique value proposition — this is one of three entrepreneurial strategies listed (pinpointing audience, crafting proposition, shaping identity).
